title: Canonical Form Uniqueness Conditions

basis.scope: Canonical bounded uniqueness semantics for REDUCE_025 outcomes after deterministic termination is established, including canonical representatives, normal-form equivalence classes, and bounded uniqueness modulo process equivalence without asserting a universal uniqueness proof.

core_rule.statement: Uniqueness is bounded by deterministic reduction and finite termination; canonical representatives are selected only from NF(C); process equivalence governs canonical-form comparison; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the bounded conditions under which the canonical normal form of a continuation is unique modulo process equivalence. This patch establishes uniqueness semantics without asserting a universal uniqueness proof.

canonical_claims.statement: Canonical form uniqueness is bounded by deterministic reduction and finite termination.
Canonical representatives are selected only after successful termination into NF(C).
Bounded uniqueness does not imply global confluence.
Equivalent traces do not affect representative selection.

formal_objects.name: Canonical Form Uniqueness
formal_objects.definition: A property indicating that a continuation possesses a unique canonical normal form modulo process equivalence.

formal_objects.name: Canonical Representative
formal_objects.definition: The selected representative of a process-equivalence class after lawful reduction.

formal_objects.name: Normal Form Equivalence Class
formal_objects.definition: The equivalence class of all canonical normal forms related by process equivalence.

formal_objects.name: Uniqueness Class
formal_objects.definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to bounded canonical-form uniqueness.

requirements: All lawful reductions produce process-equivalent canonical forms
Canonical representative is uniquely determined modulo ≡P

canonical_statement.rule: If Det(C) ∧ Term(C), then NF(C) is unique modulo ≡P for the bounded continuation class.

canonical_representative_rules: Rep(C) is selected only after successful termination.

invariants: Uniqueness does not imply global confluence.

Process equivalence remains the governing equivalence relation.
